summary: Audited 155 existing Dairy & Eggs items. The category is strong on cheeses (cheddar, brie, gouda, feta, parmesan, etc.), creams (heavy/light/single/double/whipping/clotted/table), cultured dairy (kefir, crème fraîche, quark, skyr, mascarpone, ricotta, paneer, sour cream), milks (whole/2%/1%, lactose-free, evaporated, powdered, non-dairy variants), and eggs (chicken/duck/quail/goose/turkey plus husbandry labels). However it skews heavily toward US/Western-European products and has notable global gaps: NO sweetened condensed milk, NO half-and-half, NO labneh, NO burrata/queso fresco/queso Oaxaca/queso blanco/queso de bola, NO comté/edam/jarlsberg/raclette/taleggio/camembert/chèvre/halloumi/mizithra/kashkaval as distinct items (most live only as aliases under the generic 'cheese' catch-all), NO ayran/lassi/doogh drinkable yogurts, NO filmjölk/viili/amasi/leben, NO A2/raw/UHT/condensed-milk milk variants, NO ghee distinct from butterfat clarified, NO eggnog. Data-quality issues: several items carry WRONG-product aliases (e.g. 'goat milk yogurt' aliased as 'goatmilk'/'lait de chèvre' = the milk not the yogurt; 'nonfat cottage cheese' aliased 'nonfat yogurt'; 'low fat buttermilk' aliased 'low-fat yogurt'; 'skyr plain' aliased plain yogurts; 'crema sour cream' & 'nacho cheese sauce' both alias generic 'queso/sour creams'). Vegan/non-dairy items inconsistently tagged: 'non-dairy milk' parent is tagged Vegetarian with allergens:['dairy'] (contradictory), and several plant items lack Vegan. The generic 'cheese' item is an alias dumping ground (~90 aliases) that masks dozens of distinct cheeses that deserve their own child items. Proposing 58 new items (mostly global cheeses, cultured dairy, and milk forms) plus alias and cleanup fixes.
issues: The generic 'cheese' item holds ~90 aliases including many distinct named cheeses (camembert, edam, emmenthaler, gruyère, jarlsberg, raclette, taleggio, chèvre, halloumi, oaxaca, panela, fresco, neufchatel, stilton, roquefort, boursin, burrata, ricotta salata, paneer, etc.). These should become first-class child items of 'cheese' rather than aliases, so users can track them individually.
MISSING staple: sweetened condensed milk — extremely common pantry/baking item, distinct from evaporated milk (sugar added, ~40-45%). Not present at all.
MISSING staple: half-and-half — one of the most common US dairy items, absent (only heavy/light/single/double/whipping/table cream exist).
MISSING: labneh (strained yogurt cheese, Middle Eastern) — major cultured-dairy gap given quark/skyr/crème fraîche are catalogued.
MISSING drinkable/regional cultured dairy: ayran, doogh, lassi, filmjölk, viili, amasi/maas, leben, dahi/curd, matsoni — none present despite kefir being well covered.
MISSING egg forms: liquid egg whites, liquid whole eggs, dried/powdered egg, century egg / salted duck egg (Asian preserved), eggnog. Ostrich egg also absent from the bird-egg set.

MISSING milk forms/sources: A2 milk, raw milk, UHT/shelf-stable milk, sheep's milk (drinking), camel milk, condensed milk (sweetened), chocolate/flavored milk, fat-free/skim drinking milk as an explicit child of 'milk' (only powdered-skim and lactose-free-skim exist).

MISSING cheese categories: cottage-cheese has curd-size children but no 'whipped/blended cottage cheese'; no farmer cheese / pot cheese as distinct (only an alias); no fresh chèvre log; no feta brine variants; no processed-cheese-slice generic; no parmesan rind; no cheese curds (squeaky, poutine) as distinct from generic.

Husbandry/marketing egg labels (cage-free, free-range, organic, omega-3) are modeled as sibling child items of 'egg' rather than as facets — this is acceptable but inconsistent with the facet system used elsewhere (e.g. milk fat %). Noted, not blocking.

TAG inconsistency: 'non-dairy milk' (parent) is tagged ['Vegetarian','Gluten-Free','Nut-Free'] with allergens:['dairy'] — contradictory; a plant milk should be Vegan/Dairy-Free and not carry a dairy allergen. Its children (almond/soy/oat/etc.) are correctly Vegan but the parent is not.
TAG inconsistency: 'goat milk yogurt' is missing 'Vegetarian' (has only Gluten-Free, Nut-Free) while every other yogurt/dairy item is Vegetarian.
TAG gap: 'vegan cream cheese' is correctly Vegan but is parented to 'cream-cheese' (a dairy item) — child of a dairy parent but Vegan; semantically odd, though tolerable for substitution logic.

NAMING: several child items have terse machine-y names that read awkwardly in UI: 'cream double' (vs 'double cream'), 'butter cultured' (vs 'cultured butter'), 'buttermilk cultured', 'crème fraîche cultured', 'crème fraîche double', 'cream cheese double', 'kefir plain', 'quark plain', 'skyr plain', 'yogurt flavored', 'quark flavored', 'kefir flavored'. The human-readable form is usually already in aliases; consider swapping name/alias.
'whole milk' aliases include 'whole-milk yogurt' — that is a yogurt, not milk; mis-tagged alias.

evaporated-milk has children with inconsistent storage: parent 'evaporated milk' is Pantry but child 'evaporated milk 2%' is Refrigerated, while 'whole evaporated milk' is Pantry. Unopened evaporated milk is shelf-stable; the 2% child storage looks wrong.

'pudding', 'custard', 'flan', 'creme anglaise', 'pastry cream', 'banana/butterscotch/tapioca pudding' are arguably prepared desserts rather than raw dairy ingredients — borderline for a pantry catalog, but harmless. Noted.

CROSS-CATEGORY overlap: a few dairy/egg products already live in OTHER categories — 'sweetened condensed milk' (id sweetened-condensed-milk, Canned & Jarred), 'chocolate milk' (id chocolate-milk, Beverages), 'eggnog' (id eggnog, Beverages). They are proposed here for taxonomic completeness, but the maintainer should decide whether to recategorize them under Dairy & Eggs or leave them; do NOT create true duplicate ids.
redundancies: 'crema sour cream' (id=crema) duplicates 'sour cream' and even shares the exact same aliases ['sour creams','sourcreams']. Mexican crema is slightly thinner/tangier; if kept it should be a distinct child with its own aliases, otherwise merge into sour-cream.

'nacho cheese sauce' (id=nacho) is a child of cheese-sauce but copies cheese-sauce's own aliases ['cheese sauces','queso']; those generic aliases belong on the parent only. Nacho should keep just nacho-specific aliases.

Top-level 'paneer' and child 'malai paneer' share IDENTICAL aliases ['fresh paneer','indian cottage cheese','paneers']. The generic aliases should live only on the parent 'paneer'; malai (cream) paneer should have distinct aliases or none.

'cottage cheese' aliases include 'paneer (loose)' and 'farmers cheese', while 'paneer' is its own top-level item. Cross-aliasing paneer onto cottage cheese is redundant/confusing now that paneer exists independently.

'whipped cream' and 'dairy free whipped cream' share identical aliases ['aerosol cream','chantilly cream','whipped creams']. Generic aliases should stay on the dairy parent; the dairy-free child should not claim them.

'heavy cream' (alias 'double cream') and 'whipping cream' overlap heavily in US usage (heavy >=36% fat, whipping ~30-36%). Both legitimately distinct, but 'double cream' alias on heavy collides with the separate 'cream double' item — pick one home for 'double cream'.
'cream double' (child of cream) and 'heavy cream' (alias 'double cream') represent the same UK/US product split; the 'double cream' name/alias is duplicated across two items.
'powdered milk skim' copies ALL of powdered-milk's aliases ['dry milk','instant milk','milk powder','powdered milks'] plus 'skim milk'. The shared generic aliases belong only on the parent.
'colby cheese' aliases 'colby-jack cheese', but 'colby jack string cheese' (id=colby-jack) is a separate item. The 'colby-jack' alias on colby overlaps the dedicated colby-jack item.
'neufchâtel cream cheese' is a child of cream-cheese, but 'cream cheese' itself lists 'neufchatel' as an alias — redundant; remove the alias from the parent since the child exists.

newItems.name: sweetened condensed milk
newItems.notes: Milk reduced with ~40-45% added sugar; baking/dessert staple worldwide (dulce de leche, Vietnamese coffee, tres leches). Unopened cans shelf-stable 18-24 months; ~1-2 weeks refrigerated once opened. NOTE: already exists as id 'sweetened-condensed-milk' in category 'Canned & Jarred' — decide whether to recategorize into Dairy & Eggs or skip to avoid a cross-category duplicate.

newItems.name: half-and-half
newItems.notes: US blend of equal parts whole milk and cream (~10-18% fat); ubiquitous coffee/cooking dairy. Major gap.

newItems.name: skim milk
newItems.notes: Drinking skim/fat-free milk; existing catalog only has powdered-skim and lactose-free-skim, not the plain liquid.

newItems.name: A2 milk
newItems.notes: Milk from cows producing only A2 beta-casein; marketed for easier digestion; growing US/AU/NZ category.

newItems.name: raw milk
newItems.notes: Unpasteurized cow/goat milk; shorter shelf life. Common in farm/homestead and parts of Europe.

newItems.name: UHT milk
newItems.notes: Ultra-heat-treated aseptic milk; sold shelf-stable, dominant format in much of Europe/Asia/Latin America.

newItems.name: chocolate milk
newItems.notes: Sweetened/flavored dairy milk; common grocery staple. NOTE: already exists as id 'chocolate-milk' in category 'Beverages' — recategorize/parent under 'milk' or skip to avoid a cross-category duplicate.

newItems.name: sheep's milk
newItems.notes: Drinking sheep's milk (only sheep's-milk ricotta exists today); base for feta, pecorino, Roquefort, manchego.

newItems.name: camel milk
newItems.notes: Middle East, North/East Africa, South Asia staple; niche but global premium product.

newItems.name: labneh
newItems.notes: Middle Eastern/Levantine strained yogurt cheese; major cultured-dairy gap given quark and skyr are present.

newItems.name: ayran
newItems.notes: Turkish/Middle Eastern salted yogurt-and-water drink (doogh is the Persian carbonated/herbed version).

newItems.name: lassi
newItems.notes: Indian subcontinent yogurt drink, sweet or salted/spiced (chaas is the thin spiced version).

newItems.name: dahi
newItems.notes: South Asian set curd/yogurt; the everyday 'curd' of Indian cooking. ('curd' is currently only a generic yogurt alias.)

newItems.name: filmjölk
newItems.notes: Swedish/Nordic mesophilic fermented milk (viili is the Finnish stretchy cousin); breakfast staple in Scandinavia.

newItems.name: amasi
newItems.notes: Southern African fermented soured milk (amasi/maas); leben/laban is the comparable Levantine/North African cultured milk.

newItems.name: eggnog
newItems.notes: Seasonal milk/cream/egg/sugar beverage; common US/UK/Latin (rompope/coquito kin) winter dairy product. NOTE: already exists as id 'eggnog' in category 'Beverages' — likely keep there; listed here only for completeness of the dairy/egg taxonomy.

newItems.name: liquid egg whites
newItems.notes: Cartoned pasteurized egg whites; baking/fitness staple.

newItems.name: liquid whole eggs
newItems.notes: Pasteurized liquid whole egg in carton; common foodservice/home item distinct from shell eggs.

newItems.name: powdered eggs
newItems.notes: Shelf-stable dehydrated egg for baking/camping/emergency stores.

newItems.name: century egg
newItems.notes: Chinese alkaline-preserved duck/chicken egg; congee/appetizer staple in East Asia.

newItems.name: salted duck egg
newItems.notes: Brine-cured duck egg; key in Chinese/SE-Asian cooking (mooncakes, congee, salted-egg sauces).

newItems.name: ostrich egg
newItems.notes: Largest culinary egg (~24 chicken eggs); rounds out the bird-egg set alongside duck/quail/goose/turkey.

newItems.name: burrata
newItems.notes: Italian (Puglia) fresh cheese: mozzarella shell filled with stracciatella and cream. Very short shelf life. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: queso fresco
newItems.notes: Mild crumbly fresh Mexican cheese; ubiquitous in Latin cooking. Currently only a 'cheese' alias ('fresco cheese').

newItems.name: queso Oaxaca
newItems.notes: Mexican semi-soft stringy melting cheese (mozzarella-like); for quesadillas. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: panela cheese
newItems.notes: Fresh Mexican cow's-milk cheese that holds shape when heated. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: halloumi
newItems.notes: Cypriot brined sheep/goat (often + cow) cheese with high melting point; grills/fries without melting. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: camembert
newItems.notes: French soft bloomy-rind cheese; sibling to brie. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: comté
newItems.notes: French alpine hard cow's-milk cheese (Jura); nutty, great melter. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: edam
newItems.notes: Dutch semi-hard waxed cheese. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: jarlsberg
newItems.notes: Norwegian mild holey cheese. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: raclette
newItems.notes: Swiss/French alpine melting cheese eaten scraped over potatoes. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: taleggio
newItems.notes: Italian washed-rind semi-soft cheese. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: stilton
newItems.notes: English PDO blue cheese. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: roquefort
newItems.notes: French sheep's-milk blue (PDO). Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: ricotta salata
newItems.notes: Pressed, salted, aged ricotta — firm and gratable; distinct from soft ricotta. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: boursin
newItems.notes: French Gournay soft garlic-and-herb spreadable cheese. Currently only a 'cheese' alias.

newItems.name: mizithra
newItems.notes: Greek whey cheese (fresh soft or aged hard/grating); classic over browned-butter pasta. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: kashkaval
newItems.notes: Balkan/Eastern-Mediterranean pasta-filata yellow cheese (kasseri is the Greek cousin). Missing entirely.

newItems.name: queso de bola
newItems.notes: Filipino festive Edam-style waxed ball cheese (Noche Buena). Missing entirely.

newItems.name: limburger
newItems.notes: Belgian/German washed-rind strong-smelling cheese. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: wensleydale
newItems.notes: English crumbly cow's-milk cheese (often with cranberries). Missing entirely.

newItems.name: red leicester
newItems.notes: English orange cheddar-type cheese. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: double gloucester
newItems.notes: English semi-hard cow's-milk cheese. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: fromage blanc
newItems.notes: French fresh soft cheese, quark/cottage-cheese family; mild tangy spread. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: farmer cheese
newItems.notes: Pressed, drier fresh curd cheese (Eastern-European tvorog); used in pierogi/blintzes/cheesecake. Currently only aliases on cheese/cottage-cheese.

newItems.name: cheese curds
newItems.notes: Fresh young cheddar curds (poutine, fried curds); Quebec/US-Midwest staple. Currently only an alias on 'cheese'.

newItems.name: processed cheese slices
newItems.notes: Individually-wrapped melting cheese slices; distinct from block American. Currently only generic 'cheese' aliases.

newItems.name: grana padano
newItems.notes: Italian hard grating cheese, milder/cheaper Parmigiano alternative. Currently folded into parmesan aliases.

newItems.name: queso de cabra
newItems.notes: Spanish/Latin aged goat cheese. Rounds out goat-cheese family beyond fresh chèvre.

newItems.name: kashk
newItems.notes: Persian/Central-Asian dried fermented whey or drained-yogurt product; used in kashk-e bademjan. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: smetana
newItems.notes: Eastern-European high-fat sour cream; richer than US sour cream. Missing entirely.

newItems.name: rompope
newItems.notes: Mexican/Latin egg-and-milk custard drink (coquito is the Puerto Rican coconut version); seasonal. Bottled forms shelf-stable.

newItems.name: clabber milk
newItems.notes: Traditional naturally-soured raw milk; old US South/Appalachian and global cultured-milk staple.

newItems.name: buffalo milk
newItems.notes: Drinking water-buffalo milk (only 'buffalo milk ricotta' exists today); base for mozzarella di bufala and South-Asian dairy.

newItems.name: vegan butter
newItems.notes: Plant-based butter alternative; mirrors the existing vegan-cream-cheese / dairy-free-whipped-cream non-dairy entries.

newItems.name: vegan cheese
newItems.notes: Plant-based cheese analog; currently only 'soy cheese'/'vegan cheese' aliases under generic cheese.

newItems.name: pea non dairy creamer
newItems.notes: Refrigerated liquid plant-based coffee creamer (oat/soy/pea); complements the shelf-stable flavored non-dairy creamers.

cleanups.fix: Fix contradictory tagging on the parent: remove allergens ['dairy'] (it is a plant milk) and add 'Vegan' + 'Dairy-Free' to dietaryTags to match its children (almond/soy/oat etc.).

Add 'Vegetarian' to dietaryTags (currently only Gluten-Free, Nut-Free) for consistency with all other yogurt/dairy items. Also remove milk aliases ('caprine milk','chèvre milk','goatmilk','lait de chèvre') — this item is goat-milk YOGURT, not goat milk; those aliases describe the milk and should move to a goat-milk (drinking) item or be dropped.
Remove wrong alias 'nonfat yogurt' (this is cottage cheese, not yogurt).
Remove wrong alias 'low-fat yogurt' (this item is low-fat BUTTERMILK).
Remove aliases 'low-fat plain yogurt'/'nonfat plain yogurt' — these describe generic plain yogurt, not skyr specifically; they belong on the 'yogurt' parent.
Remove alias 'whole-milk yogurt' (a yogurt, not whole milk); move to the yogurt item if desired.

Either merge into 'sour-cream' or give it crema-specific aliases ('mexican crema','crema mexicana','table cream crema'); it currently just duplicates sour-cream's aliases ['sour creams','sourcreams'].
Remove the parent's generic aliases ['cheese sauces','queso']; keep only nacho-specific aliases ('nacho cheese','nacho sauce').
Remove the duplicated generic paneer aliases ['fresh paneer','indian cottage cheese','paneers']; keep only 'malai paneer'/'cream paneer'. Generic aliases belong on the 'paneer' parent.
Remove cross-product aliases 'paneer (loose)' and 'farmers cheese' now that 'paneer' exists independently and 'farmer cheese' is proposed as its own item.

Remove the dairy whipped-cream aliases ['aerosol cream','chantilly cream','whipped creams']; those belong on the dairy 'whipped-cream' parent. This dairy-free child should not claim generic whipped-cream search terms.
Remove the duplicated parent aliases ['dry milk','instant milk','milk powder','powdered milks']; keep only 'skim milk powder'/'nonfat dry milk'. Generics belong on 'powdered-milk'.
Remove 'neufchatel' from the cream-cheese PARENT's aliases since this dedicated neufchâtel child exists (avoids the alias and the item competing).
Remove alias 'colby-jack cheese' — there is a dedicated colby-jack item; this colby (plain) item should not also claim colby-jack.
Set defaultStorage to 'Pantry' to match the evaporated-milk parent and whole-evaporated-milk sibling (unopened evaporated milk is shelf-stable); current 'Refrigerated' is inconsistent.

Prune the ~90-alias dumping ground: promote distinct named cheeses to first-class child items (camembert, edam, emmenthaler, gruyère, jarlsberg, raclette, taleggio, stilton, roquefort, boursin, burrata, ricotta-salata, oaxaca, panela, fresco, halloumi, paneer, neufchatel, soy/vegan cheese, cheese curds, processed slices — many proposed above). Keep only true spelling-variant aliases (chedder, mozarella, parmesean) and broad generics (block cheese, hard cheese, melting cheese) on the parent.

Resolve the duplicate 'double cream' representation: 'cream double' (child) and 'heavy cream' (alias 'double cream') both claim it. Pick one canonical home (recommend keeping 'double cream' as a child item and removing the alias from heavy-cream), and consider renaming 'cream double' -> 'double cream' for readability.

Rename 'butter cultured' -> 'cultured butter' (the readable form, already an alias) for UI clarity. Same pattern applies to buttermilk-cultured, crème-fraîche-cultured, crème-fraîche-double, cream-cheese-double, kefir-plain, quark-plain, skyr-plain, yogurt-flavored, quark-flavored, kefir-flavored.
